name: Cyan (Process)
lede: Cyan (Process) is the bright, greenish blue standardized as one of the four printing inks in the CMYK model, named to distinguish it from other, differently-defined cyans.

sections.title: One of four printing inks
sections.body: Our record of this name traces to Wikipedia's article on the CMYK color model, where process cyan is one of the four standard printing inks, alongside magenta, yellow and black [1]. The "(Process)" label distinguishes it from other colors also called cyan, such as web or additive-light cyan, which are defined differently and can look a little different on screen [1]. Its nearest named neighbors by color distance are [[deep-sky-blue|Deep Sky Blue]], almost the same hue at 3.6 units, and [[maximum-blue|Maximum Blue]], [[bright-sky-blue|Bright Sky Blue]] and [[cyan-blue|Cyan blue]], each a little duller, lighter or bluer, all within about 5.4 to 6.6 units [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color this close to Cyan (Process) is essentially absent from our archive: only one of 23,781 paintings carries it, as photographed, and not even enough of that canvas to count by our within-painting measure [3]. That is expected: process cyan is a printing standard, not a historical pigment, so painters before modern printing had no reason to mix it [3].
